title: CYBRIK F8 receipt integrity signature profile proposal v1
description: A candidate answer to the receipt-signing envelope that ADR-0004 F8 deferred, offered contract-first so the choice can be reviewed against real bytes instead of a paragraph. The packet adds two schemas — a signed statement and a transport envelope — plus a frozen, cryptographically reproducible Ed25519 test vector and a rejection inventory. It reuses the accepted cybrik.execution-receipt.v1 and cybrik.common-defs.v1 by $ref and changes no byte of either. Status: PROPOSED — NOT ACCEPTED (v0.1.0; not stable v1/GA) — NOT IMPLEMENTED. This packet records no ADR decision, closes no ADR-0004 deferral, authorizes no issuer, signer, key lifecycle, ledger or runtime, and grants no release authority.

ownership.fabric: Sole owner of the receipt-signing decision, the signing key, and the receipt ledger. The Tool Fabric control plane signs; an executor attests evidence INTO a receipt and never holds a receipt-signing key (ADR-0004 F6; ADR-0006 E5). A receipt is therefore a control-plane observation of an execution, not an executor's self-report about it.
ownership.cyber_ai: May read and verify a receipt. It cannot mint, sign, countersign, or amend one, and a model may never be an input to a signing decision.
ownership.soc: May read and verify a receipt under SOC-owned tenant and analyst truth. It cannot mint or sign one.
ownership.suite: Owns this proposed cross-product contract packet and its static conformance evidence only. It gains no product-runtime, signing, key-management, or release authority.

digest_profile.recipe: Take the exact transmitted receipt. Remove exactly the two top-level keys receipt_digest and signature, and nothing else. Inject no schema default. Canonicalize the remainder with RFC 8785 JCS. The hash input is UTF-8('CYBRIK-RECEIPT-JCS/v1') then one 0x00 byte then the JCS bytes; receipt_digest is 'sha256:' plus the lowercase hex SHA-256 of that input.
digest_profile.profile_binding_rationale: The profile id sits inside the hash input, separated by a NUL that cannot occur in the JCS bytes. A verifier therefore cannot be tricked into accepting a digest computed under a weaker or different recipe by being handed a different profile label alongside the same bytes.
digest_profile.no_default_injection_rationale: cybrik.execution-receipt.v1 declares `default: []` on input_artifact_digests and output_artifacts. Materializing either before hashing would make 'the control plane observed no output artifacts' and 'the control plane observed an empty list of output artifacts' sign to the same digest, so a defaults-normalized rewrite of a receipt would verify against the original signature. The frozen test vector omits output_artifacts and the examples manifest pins both digests to keep that distinction provable rather than asserted.

signature_profile.serialization: Ordinary JWS compact serialization with an INCLUDED payload: three non-empty unpadded base64url segments. Detached payloads and RFC 7797 b64=false are rejected, so the bytes a verifier hashes are always the bytes it was given.
signature_profile.algorithm: EdDSA over Ed25519 only. alg=none and every other algorithm are rejected.
signature_profile.payload: The RFC 8785 JCS rendering of cybrik.receipt-signature-statement.v1. Canonical rendering of both the header and the payload is what makes the frozen vector byte-reproducible from the statement alone.
signature_profile.key_resolution: kid resolves ONLY against a pinned external trust bundle. jwk, jku, x5u, x5c, x5t, x5t#S256 and epk are forbidden in the protected header — the exact-key-set rule already excludes them, and they are enumerated so a violation names the specific attack. bundle_uri is a pinned identifier, never a fetch instruction; a verifier that cannot match bundle_digest against a bundle it already trusts fails closed.
signature_profile.kid_grammar: cybrik-receipt-signer:v1:<64 lowercase hex>, where the hex is the SHA-256 over the RFC 7638 thumbprint input for an OKP key — the JCS rendering of exactly {crv, kty, x}. RFC 7638 renders that digest as base64url; rendering it as hex is this profile's only deliberate divergence, taken so the kid grammar stays a single character class.
signature_profile.signature_locator: cybrik-ledger://receipt-signatures/sha256/<64 lowercase hex>, where the hex is the SHA-256 of the exact compact JWS bytes. It is a content address, and it is exactly the string the receipt's own `signature` field carries.

rejection_inventory.rule: The declared digest profile must be CYBRIK-RECEIPT-JCS/v1 with canonicalization RFC8785-JCS on both the envelope and the signed statement, and the declared receipt_digest must equal the digest recomputed from the exact transmitted receipt with only receipt_digest and signature removed and no schema default injected.
signature_locator must match cybrik-ledger://receipt-signatures/sha256/<64 lowercase hex> and the hex must equal the SHA-256 of the exact compact JWS bytes.

The compact JWS must have exactly three non-empty strict base64url segments (payload included, never detached), and the protected header must decode to a JSON object whose key set is exactly {alg, kid, typ} with the pinned typ and a kid matching every other kid in the envelope and statement.
alg must be EdDSA over an OKP/Ed25519 key in both the protected header and the envelope. alg=none and every other algorithm are rejected, as is b64=false.

No embedded or remote key may appear anywhere: jwk, jku, x5u, x5c, x5t, x5t#S256 and epk are forbidden in the header, no key material may appear in the envelope, and kid resolves only against the pinned external trust bundle.

The decoded payload must be byte-identical to the JCS rendering of its own parse, must deep-equal the signed-statement member, and must bind the same receipt_id and recomputed receipt_digest as the envelope and the receipt.
The signature segment must be exactly 64 bytes and must verify as Ed25519 over the ASCII bytes of "<protected>.<payload>" under the trust-bundle public key selected by kid.

runtime_invariants: A receipt is a CONTROL-PLANE OBSERVATION of an execution, not an executor attestation about one. The control plane signs; an executor contributes evidence that the control plane records. A signature therefore proves what the control plane recorded, and never that an executor behaved as recorded.
A receipt-signing key never exists on an executor, in a sandbox, in a model runtime, or in the SOC (ADR-0004 F6; ADR-0006 E5).
Verification is offline and fail-closed: a verifier resolves kid in a trust bundle it already holds, and rejects rather than fetching anything named in the message.

The digest covers the exact transmitted receipt bytes with no normalization beyond removing the two self-referential fields, so no proxy, serializer, or storage layer may re-render a receipt and keep its signature valid.
Signature validity says nothing about authorization. Who was allowed to run the action remains the policy decision, approval, and digest-bound delegation chain the receipt itself binds.
authority_invariants: This packet grants no capability, invocation, approval, credential, egress, sandbox, or MCP authority.
This packet neither creates nor names a production signer, issuer, ledger, endpoint, or key store.
A model or an agent may never be an input to a signing decision or a trust-bundle change.
Nothing here permits an executor to produce, countersign, or amend a receipt signature.

future_prerequisites.statement: ADR-0004 F5 single-use, scoped, short-lived credential leases are not designed or built. cybrik.execution-receipt.v1 already carries credential_lease_id_hash, but nothing mints, scopes, or expires the lease it hashes, so the field is currently an unbacked promise. A signature over it proves only that the control plane wrote that hash.

ADR-0004 F4 executor workload attestation is deferred. executor.id is a SPIFFE-shaped string the control plane recorded, not an attested identity that was cryptographically proven at execution time. Until attestation exists, a receipt binds WHICH executor the control plane believed it dispatched to, not which one actually ran.

No production issuer, signing service, HSM or KMS placement, availability posture, or signing-authorization policy is selected. The only key in this packet is a runtime-derived TEST-ONLY value whose private half is trivially recomputable, and it exists solely to make the fixture reproducible.

Key generation, rotation, revocation, trust-bundle distribution and freshness, cross-rotation verification of historical receipts, and compromise recovery are entirely undesigned. This is the largest single gap: the profile pins how a signature is shaped, and says nothing about how the key behind it is governed over time.

open_decisions.question: Adopt a JWS-shaped receipt-signing envelope at all, rather than COSE or an in-toto-style statement?
open_decisions.current: OPEN — this packet argues one side by making it concrete. Under the active delegated-governor authority, the comparison and technical choice remain the Codex Governor's; no alternative was prototyped here.

open_decisions.question: Accept RFC 8785 JCS as the canonicalization, given that it fixes number and string rendering to the JSON grammar and cannot express a non-JSON receipt?
open_decisions.current: OPEN — JCS is chosen here because the corpus already renders canonical JSON this way; no other canonicalization was measured.

open_decisions.question: Accept a hex-rendered RFC 7638 thumbprint as the kid, diverging from the base64url rendering the RFC specifies?
open_decisions.current: OPEN — the divergence buys a single-character-class grammar and costs a small interoperability surprise for off-the-shelf JOSE tooling.

open_decisions.question: Accept Ed25519-only, with no negotiated algorithm agility and therefore no in-band path to a post-quantum or FIPS-track signature?
open_decisions.current: OPEN — agility is deliberately refused here because a negotiable alg is the root of the downgrade attacks RI-4 exists to block. A future profile version, not a runtime negotiation, would be the migration path.

open_decisions.question: Open a design gate for the key lifecycle and trust-bundle distribution named in future_prerequisites before, not after, any implementation of this profile?
open_decisions.current: OPEN — proposed sequencing only; no gate is opened by this packet.

verification_commands.workspace_note: Both commands run with tools/contract-validation as the working directory. The standalone validator needs no node_modules; the test suite pulls the already-pinned ajv 8.20.0 / ajv-formats 3.0.1 from the local install, or from the directory named by CYBRIK_CONTRACT_VALIDATION_DEPS_ROOT. This packet installs nothing, adds no dependency, and reaches no network.
verification_commands.orchestrator_registration: REGISTERED — validate-receipt-integrity.mjs is a step in tools/contract-validation/validate.mjs and both commands are package.json scripts. Registration is local orchestration only: no CI pipeline was run, no CI result is claimed, and the test file is deliberately NOT added to W1_CONTRACT_TEST_FILES so the pinned W1 contract-test count is unchanged.

x-cybrik-packet-integrity.file_digest_rule: Every member except this manifest is digested as the lowercase hex SHA-256 of the exact on-disk UTF-8 bytes of '<path_root><file>'.
x-cybrik-packet-integrity.self_digest_rule: This manifest's own member digest is deliberately NOT taken over its on-disk bytes. It is the lowercase hex SHA-256 of the UTF-8 encoding of JSON.stringify(this manifest parsed as JSON with the top-level 'x-cybrik-packet-integrity' key removed). Because the hashed input excludes the integrity block, no digest input ever contains a digest, which is what makes the self entry and the aggregate below non-circular and independently reproducible. Consequence, stated deliberately: for this one member the digest pins the JSON value, not the on-disk byte formatting.
x-cybrik-packet-integrity.aggregate_algorithm: Sort all 10 member entries ascending by 'file' using JavaScript default string comparison, render each entry as the line '<sha256>  <file>' (two spaces), join the lines with a single '\n' and no trailing newline, then take the lowercase hex SHA-256 of the UTF-8 encoding of that string. The aggregate consumes only the 10 member digests, so it never depends on its own value.

gate.decision_authority: Codex Governor under docs/operations/DELEGATED-GOVERNOR-AUTHORITY-2026-07-30.md. A separately recorded technical decision is still required to select a receipt-signing envelope; this packet is input to that decision and is not a substitute for it. Production remains Founder-controlled.
gate.what_green_validation_proves: That the proposed profile is internally consistent, that its frozen vector verifies as Ed25519, and that its declared rejection inventory really rejects. Static conformance only.
gate.what_green_validation_does_not_prove: That this is the right envelope, that any alternative is worse, that a signer exists, that a key can be rotated, that a receipt is durably recorded, or that an executor behaved as a receipt says. None of the four future_prerequisites is addressed by any check in this packet; receipt-ledger durability remains a separate open runtime obligation.
